composerInfo.name: Alexander Scriabin
composerInfo.hook: Alexander Nikolayevich Scriabin was a Russian composer and pianist.
composerInfo.bio: Initially influenced by Frédéric Chopin, he composed in a relatively tonal, late-Romantic idiom. Later, independently of his contemporary Arnold Schoenberg, Scriabin developed a highly dissonant musical language that transcended traditional tonality without being strictly atonal, aligning with his personal brand of metaphysics. He embraced the concepts of Gesamtkunstwerk and synesthesia, creating a colour-coded circle of fifths inspired by theosophy to associate colours with harmonies. Scriabin is widely considered the primary Russian symbolist composer and a major figure of the Silver Age of Russian Poetry.

He embraced the concepts of Gesamtkunstwerk and synesthesia, creating a colour-coded circle of fifths inspired by theosophy to associate colours with harmonies. advice: Right hand leaps up an octave — C#5 to C#6. Practise the jump silently first: eyes find C#6 before the hand leaves C#5, then add sound once the distance feels automatic.
Right hand chord A3+C#4+C#5+C#6 spans an octave plus a 10th — if the reach is too wide, roll it gently from A3 up, landing C#6 exactly on the beat.
Syncopation — C#5, G#5, E#5, F#5 land between the beats. Tap a steady pulse with one hand and say the rhythm out loud before playing it.
Finger 1 lands on F#4, a black key — move the whole hand slightly into the keys so the thumb reaches it without twisting.
Mostly black keys here (C#5, C#6, C#4) — play nearer the fallboard where the black keys sit, with firm curved fingertips.
